- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to over-forecast (especially after spikes), so reduce forecast by 5–15% for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >15% from prior 10-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias of 10–20% for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags in adjusting — forecast should be adjusted toward historical mean or recent 7-day average within 2–4 days.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to over-forecast the mean — use 30-day moving average as baseline and adjust downward if sentiment is weak or volatile.  
- For long-term (30-day) forecasts, model often overestimates volatility — cap forecast at 1.5x recent 30-day average unless sentiment strongly bullish.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive and price is trending down, model may misread sentiment — reduce forecast by 5–10% for 3–7 days to avoid “sentiment overfitting.”
